J0–J3 contain 126, 163, 134 and 95 distinct proteins, respectively. Paired 95% intervals use 2,000 protein-clustered resamples within each fixed cell: sampled proteins contribute all their variants, with the same multiplicities for both models. Percentile intervals condition on the fitted ensembles and graph; they do not include retraining, graph-sampling or subgroup-selection uncertainty and are not adjusted for multiple comparisons. All 2,000 resamples were evaluable in the four displayed cells. The low-k-core/mid-betweenness, low-k-core/high-betweenness, low-k-core/high-clustering and mid-neighbour-risk/low-k-core cells had 2, 227, 95 and 724 single-class resamples, respectively; their undefined AUC/AP differences were excluded from the corresponding percentile intervals, without replacement draws. Full point estimates, protein counts, finite-replicate counts, intervals and memberships for all 53 cells, together with the 18 one-dimensional strata, are supplied in the compact source-data archive. These exploratory profiles do not independently confirm topology-defined benefit subgroups.

before: **Unified current reporting.** Tables 11–17, the current matched results reported in the main text and the external/network comparisons in main Figure 5 use a single post-processing convention. Main Figure 1B–D/F, Figure 2B/C/E and the matched-ensemble analysis in Figure 4 use this convention; Figure 1E, Figure 2D and Figure 3 retain their separate sensitivity or reference-fit estimates and protocols. For all 21 protein-only representation checkpoints, CPU evaluation in float32 with fixed batches of 1,024 nodes in the frozen node order produces one stored probability per protein, which is mapped to its variant rows. On the original validation/test rows, the largest difference from the earlier variant-batched probabilities was 3.58e-7; the maximum within-protein spread decreased from 2.38e-7 to exactly zero. Fusion inputs remain variant-specific. Seed probabilities are converted to float64 before averaging; all AUPRC values are non-interpolated average precision computed consistently with scikit-learn. This inference and aggregation standardization involved no model refitting or checkpoint changes. It can slightly change rank-based metrics through exact ties; earlier outputs remain archived separately rather than mixed with the current tables.
